instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Give yourself a separate virtual Mac to work in." It reads the row with do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:govijr-terminal-mac"}.

2. It checks that git, an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 14 or later, and Xcode 16 or later are on your computer, and if terminal-mac is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/govijr/terminal-mac.git ; cd terminal-mac ; bash scripts/build.sh.
3. It runs the row's command: ./dist/terminal-mac up
4. Read what it shows you. The site you asked through runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: terminal-mac on a made-up example
worked_examples.ask: Give yourself a separate virtual Mac to work in.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json: tool:github:govijr-terminal-mac runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got terminal-mac in, the command line: ./dist/terminal-mac up
worked_examples.hands_back: The build writes "dist/TerminalMac.app" (with "TerminalMacGuest.app" inside) and the "dist/terminal-mac" launcher; up then boots a separate macOS guest whose screen streams into the terminal, and the AI can screenshot, click and type in it without moving the real Mac's pointer.
